cats.name: Golden Kitty
cats.catName: The Golden Kitty, Product Hunt's trophy cat
cats.whoIsTheCat: The Golden Kitty is Product Hunt's award trophy: a chrome-gold statuette of the site's kitty mascot, wearing a Google Glass-style headset and a collar tag. At Product Hunt's first Golden Kitty Awards in December 2015, Robinhood won Sexiest Product of the Year and thanked fans on X on 23 Dec 2015. The coin is a September 2026 fan tribute on Robinhood Chain.

virality.summary: The meme rests on a real bit of startup history. Product Hunt's first Golden Kitty Awards (winners announced 22 Dec 2015) named Robinhood 'Sexiest Product of the Year', @RobinhoodApp tweeted its thanks the next day, and Robinhood's January 2016 newsroom recap listed 'the coveted Golden Kitty Award' among its 2015 highlights. Winners posted photos and videos of the trophy (Niv Dror, Mat Carpenter, Toby's @arthcmr). When memecoins arrived on Robinhood Chain in 2026, fans revived the story: GOLDEN launched on Pons on 4 Sep 2026, trades against tokenized gold ($GLD), and is now tracked by CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap, Coinbase and MEXC price pages.

cats.lore: In December 2015 Product Hunt held its first Golden Kitty Awards, and a young stock-trading app called Robinhood won Sexiest Product of the Year. The prize was a gleaming gold statuette of Product Hunt's kitty mascot, a headset over one eye and a tag on its collar. Robinhood thanked its fans the next day and the trophy went up on the shelf. Ten years later, when memecoins came to Robinhood's own chain, fans remembered the little gold cat and gave it a new home as GOLDEN, where it still sits upright and proud.

cats.name: CateCoin
cats.whoIsTheCat: Cate is CateCoin's cartoon mascot: an orange-and-white cat with a wide, open-mouthed grin. A pseudonymous team launched it on BNB Chain in May 2021 as the cat answer to Dogecoin's Shiba Inu, under the slogan 'Doge vs Cate'. No real cat is behind it.

virality.summary: CateCoin arrived in the May 2021 dog-coin mania as the cat side of 'Doge vs Cate'. It sold in Oxbull's IDO (ended 9 May 2021, $99K raised), ran a Gate.io IEO that ended 10 Nov 2021, and hit its all-time high on 9 Nov 2021. It built one of the largest cat-coin communities of that cycle and still calls itself the original cat meme coin, with staking, a meme-creator app and a Doge-vs-Cate Ludo game.

cats.lore: In the spring of 2021 the internet was full of Shiba Inu dogs, and a small anonymous team on BNB Chain asked a simple question: where are the cats? Their answer was Cate, a cheerful orange-and-white cartoon cat with a big open grin, and a coin to go with it under the banner 'Doge vs Cate'. Cate was meant for meme makers, a cat who shares the stage with the people who make the internet laugh. More than five years on, Cate is still grinning and waving a paw, now with a staking page and a Doge-vs-Cate Ludo game to play.

cats.name: Hello Kitty
cats.whoIsTheCat: Hello Kitty, real name Kitty White, is the character Yuko Shimizu created for Japan's Sanrio in 1974; she first appeared on a vinyl coin purse in March 1975. Sanrio's story makes her a kind girl from a London suburb, drawn in the motif of a white cat with a red bow and no visible mouth. This coin is an unofficial fan memecoin, not affiliated with Sanrio.

virality.summary: Hello Kitty is one of the most successful characters ever made. Wikipedia cites about $5 billion a year by 2010 and roughly $8 billion at retail in 2013, over 50,000 branded products by 2008, a UNICEF children's ambassador role, and her 2008 appointment as Japan's tourism ambassador to China and Hong Kong, the first time the ministry picked a fictional character. The coin is a small fan tribute to that fame: fan accounts @HKittyOnSol (May 2025) and @hkittycoin (November 2025) run it, and after early IP worries it switched to a plain pink bow as its logo (Bitget Wallet).

cats.lore: Hello Kitty has been saying hello since 1975, when Sanrio put a little white cat with a red bow on a vinyl coin purse in Japan, sitting between a bottle of milk and a goldfish bowl. Her story says she is Kitty White, a kind girl from a London suburb who loves baking cookies and her twin sister Mimmy. Fifty years on, a group of fans on Solana made a coin in her honour, called themselves Hello Kitty Fans and chose a simple pink bow as their badge. It is an unofficial tribute: Sanrio has nothing to do with it, and the fans say so up front.

cats.name: Cets On Gold
cats.whoIsTheCat: Cets is an original cartoon cat made for the coin: a flat, tall, golden-yellow cat with a boxy head and huge round eyes, drawn from four locked views on one model sheet. Its X bio reads 招财猫 (lucky cat, the maneki-neko of shop counters). It has lived on BNB Chain since 6 Aug 2026. The project does not name the artist who drew it.

virality.summary: Cets came out of the August 2026 BNB Chain meme season with one line: 'Every cycle, the dogs run. The cats never got their turn.' It launched on Flap on 6 Aug, listed on LBank six days later (12 Aug) and reached its CoinGecko all-time high on 30 Aug. It spreads through art more than hype: a locked four-view model sheet, 312 free downloadable artworks (270 scenes and 42 meme expressions), custom 'Cets' portraits for crypto personalities such as @CozomoMedici, @farokh and @icobeast, a Telegram sticker pack and an Instagram of short clips. A crowd of small tokens now trades against CETS on BNB Chain.

cats.lore: Cets On Gold starts with a complaint every cat lover in crypto knows: 'Every cycle, the dogs run. The cats never got their turn.' So in August 2026 a golden cat walked onto BNB Chain. Its makers drew it from four sides on one model sheet so it would always look like itself: tall, flat, boxy-headed, with enormous round eyes and a very patient face. Its bio simply says 招财猫, lucky cat. Cats have sat beside gold for thousands of years, the site reminds us, and so Cets mostly sits too: eyes closed, glowing softly in the grass, waiting its turn.
